speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng) (for the Minister for Transport)
text: Speaker, the Government is committed to helping needy commuters cope with public transport fare increases through providing them with Public Transport Vouchers (PTVs).

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng) (for the Minister for Transport)
text: We actively reach out to eligible households to encourage them to apply for the vouchers.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng) (for the Minister for Transport)
text: In addition to media announcements, we work with the People's Association to raise awareness, including distributing publicity collaterals in four languages at all Community Clubs, as well as through house visits and events.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng) (for the Minister for Transport)
text: The PTV application process allows us to directly engage and better understand each household's needs, which may go beyond transport costs.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng) (for the Minister for Transport)
text: Through this process, the CCCs have been able to provide tailored support through other Government assistance schemes.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng) (for the Minister for Transport)
text: We will continue to explore ways to streamline the process for future exercises.

speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
text: My first supplementary question is really a clarification, which is, whether there is any insight or reason for the quite large shortfall in the number of PTVs issued compared to the projected number initially.

speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
text: I am not sure that there was much insight into that at the moment.

speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
text: The second supplementary question is whether the various PT assistance schemes could be consolidated to support low-income individuals better to ensure no gaps in coverage.

speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
text: The reason is, as we have seen, the evidence suggests that right now, there may be gaps in coverage because there could be eligible families which are not coming forward for whatever reason, and it would be better to automatically give them some grants.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: The number of vouchers made available has increased over the years.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: The quantum and the numbers benefiting from the PTV exercise have also increased, although given that the fare increase typically follows a certain timeframe, for example, end of the year.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: Therefore, the PTV take-up rate may not be reflective of the economic climate or the needs of low-income households.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: We respect the decision of each household to apply for PTVs.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: When we look at the proportion, there is no discernible trend of whether it is decreasing or increasing.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: I think this depends on the individuals or the households' decision whether to apply or not.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: In fact, there are times when we advise residents to apply for certain social assistance schemes and the response is that they can cope and they do not see the need to go forth and apply for these schemes.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: Having said that, we are committed to raising awareness of the PTV exercise so that those who are in need are not deprived of it because of ignorance.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: As to the Member's second question about the consolidation of different assistance schemes, our fare structure does take care of different vulnerable groups.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: Students, senior citizens and people with disabilities also enjoy concessionary fares.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: But the needs of every individual or household could differ.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: That is why there are various other schemes available, some are automatic, some are upon application, so that tailored assistance could be made available to help these residents.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: We look forward to the local CCCs' support to help us reach out to these households so that help can be rendered to them.
